title: Tier 2 nullifier key: transcripts, dealt shares, their checks, key_id and approvals
generator: packages/crypto/scripts/nullifier-key-vectors.py: an independent Python implementation (standard library only), with keyed-nullifier-vectors.py's Baby Jubjub (checked against EIP-2494 and RFC 9380 Appendix K.1 first), share-encryption-vectors.py's ML-KEM-768 and ChaCha20-Poly1305 (checked against Go's accumulated FIPS 203 vectors and RFC 8439 first) and ristretto255, and trustee-vectors.py's P-256 ECDSA, which reproduces RFC 6979 Appendix A.2.5 first. Every value is test data, never keys

transcripts.description: Every seat of a 3-of-5 panel takes part honestly; all five qualify.
The smallest panel, 2-of-2.
Seat 5 sends nothing; the other four qualify.

Dealer 2 seals a wrong share to seat 3 (share-verify) and one that doesn't open to seat 4 (share-decrypt), and signs both hashes; seats 3 and 4 complain and dealer 2 reveals both shares correctly, so it stays qualified.
As complaint-answered, but dealer 2 reveals a wrong share for seat 3.
As complaint-answered, but dealer 2 sends no round-4 message.
Seat 4 complains about honest dealer 1 without cause: dealer 1 reveals seat 4's own share, which checks, and everyone qualifies.
Seat 3 registers keys but deals nothing; it holds no share.
Seat 5 chooses its polynomials, after seeing every other seat's share to it, so that its own share and C_5 are the identity; its dealing counts, but it holds no share.
Seat 3's signing-key signature is made by seat 1's signing key.
Seats 2 and 3 register the same signing key, each with a valid proof: both are excluded.
Seat 1 registers its own identity key as its registration signing key.
Only seats 1 and 2 take part: two qualified seats, below k = 3.
Round 1 lists seat 2 before seat 1.
Dealer 2's round-2 message is dropped after the fact, but its round-4 response stays.
Dealer 1 commits to k − 1 coefficients (signed as sent).
Seat 4 complains about itself.
Dealer 1 publishes seat 5's share though no one complained.
Seat 5, absent from round 1, complains about dealer 1 in round 3.
As complaint-answered, but seat 3 signs its complaint over h_1 instead of h_2.
As complaint-answered, but dealer 2 signs its response over h_2 instead of h_3.
Seat 1's round-1 message is swapped for another it also signed; every later message signed over the round 1 it replaced.
The run identifier is changed: every message was signed under the original context.
